title: Name the focus step in the Lore pane band line and in the skill text (seq 212, ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-43)
description:
Carry opum-doc's seq 212 ruling (ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-43, 2026-10-03T11:05:16Z; opum-doc's call under the Article 5 delegation, not the operator's) onto the Lore pane band's own line and the skill text. Recorded on opum-agent OPAG-1075 note 9, landed on opum-agent dev by opum-ai/opum-agent#1954; reread there by ref rather than taken from the routing message.

WHY. LCLI-672's findings reported that the band's `o` hotkey needs the band focused -- a bare `o` types into the composer, a bare digit presses a band Button from an empty composer, and `o` reaches this Button only after ctrl+x tab. The ruling keeps `o` (a digit would collide with other bands' Buttons and with the Lore pane link list's own digit hotkeys) and puts the focus step in the band's own line instead, so the affordance teaches its own keystroke.

WHAT THE RULING SETTLES, all three items:
1. Width floor -- NO CHANGE HERE. The engine's own `reason` is already reported verbatim; opum-doc is correcting the design doc's fixed 144 itself. Nothing in this task touches that.
2. Band hotkey -- KEEP `o`, do NOT use a digit. Render the focus step in the line, e.g. `Lore pane ready . [Open] (ctrl+x tab, o)`, and name it in the skill text where the band or hotkey is described. A click on [Open] needs no focus.
3. The amended acceptance criterion on LCLI-672 (behind-a-tab arm verified live) is accepted as written; nothing to do.

CONSISTENCY. quest-cli renders the matching line on the Quest board. Read at PR opum-ai/quest-cli#486's head (unmerged as of this task's writing; quest-cli dev does not carry it yet): `<Text>Quest board ready . </Text>`, the `Open` Button on hotkey `o`, then `<Text> (ctrl+x tab, o)</Text>`. Match that shape so the two bands read alike.

SCOPE. No version, tag, or publish work: the held LCLI-665 0.13.0 bump is untouched. The `skills/` edit ships to plugin users with the next tag, which is the point of doing it before that release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The band's single line renders the focus step at the ruled shape -- `Lore pane ready . [Open] (ctrl+x tab, o)`, with the middot and the parenthetical -- and its Button keeps hotkey `o`; no digit hotkey is introduced.

tests/pane.test.tsx pins the rendered band line: the ready text, the `(ctrl+x tab, o)` focus hint, and the Button's `Open` label and `o` hotkey all asserted, so a later edit that drops the hint goes red.
skills/lore/SKILL.md names the focus step where the pane's entry point is described -- that reaching the band's `o` needs the band focused (ctrl+x tab), while a click on [Open] needs none.
docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md's band section describes the line carrying the focus step, consistently with what the band renders.

AMENDED at closure to the measurement: `bun run lore check` exits 0 and `bun test` shows no failure this change can reach -- the one failing test (test/link-quest-race.test.ts, SF1: revision is workspace-wide) fails identically with the change stashed, as its control -- both run under the pinned bun (/opt/homebrew/bin/bun), and the gate versions are recorded in the evidence note.

implementationNotes:
EVIDENCE, LCLI-673. Branch chore/LCLI-673-band-focus-step. Versions this proof resolved: bun 1.4.2 (/opt/homebrew/bin/bun, the pinned one), claude 2.1.288 (the declaration the mod harness typechecked against), quest 0.12.0, lore from source at 0.12.0.

THE RULING WAS READ AT ITS SOURCE, not taken from the routing message. opum-agent OPAG-1075 note 9, read by `gh api repos/opum-ai/opum-agent/contents/.quest/tasks/OPAG-1075.json?ref=dev`: "RULING seq 212 (ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-43, 11:05:16Z; opum-doc's call under Article 5 delegation, not the operator's)". All three items match the relay; item 1 needs nothing here (opum-doc corrects the design doc's fixed 144 itself) and item 3 accepts the amended AC as written.

A FINDING WORTH CARRYING FORWARD, because it cost a red CI job to learn. `skills/lore/SKILL.md` is GENERATED, not hand-kept: `test/plugin-skill.test.ts` asserts the committed file is byte-identical to `buildSkillDoc("plugin")` (src/core/agent-bridge.ts). A hand-edit to SKILL.md is therefore a defect -- `bun test` went red on "the committed plugin skill is exactly the generated one". The change belongs in the generator, followed by `bun run scripts/plugin-skill.ts --write`; the regeneration then produced exactly the paragraph the hand-edit had written, which is how the two were confirmed to agree rather than assumed to. Anyone told to "document it in the skill text" should be told this too.

MUTATION CHECK, run rather than reasoned. Removing the hint element from the band (the defect's own shape: a band that draws its line without the focus step) reddened EXACTLY 1 of 57 mod tests -- "the band draws the line that offers the pane, and its Button seats what the engine would not" -- with `Expected: containing "ctrl+x tab, o" / Received: undefined`, while the other 56 stayed green. Reverted, 57 pass 0 fail. The prediction was localisation, not redness: the hint assertion is the only one that reads that Text.

GATES, all in this session. `bun run test:mod`: 57 pass, 0 fail, "The mod validates and its tests pass. Typecheck: clean." `bun run typecheck`: exit 0. `bun run lint`: exit 0, no warning in any changed file. `bun run lore check` (from source, as CI runs it): "89 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings", exit 0. `bun test`: 4921 pass, 1 skip, 1 fail.

THE ONE FAILURE IS PRE-EXISTING AND HAS A CONTROL. `test/link-quest-race.test.ts`, "SF1: revision is workspace-wide", expecting the installed quest's revision not to be workspace-wide. Run against the PRE-FIX tree in the same session -- the five changed files stashed with `git stash push -- <paths>`, run, then popped -- it fails identically there: 2 pass, 1 fail, same test, same assertion. The pair is the evidence; the post-fix run alone would not have been. No file this change touches is in that test's reach.

NO CHANGELOG ENTRY, deliberately: the Unreleased section is written at bump time in this repository -- `git log -- CHANGELOG.md` shows the last three entries landing with bump or feature commits, and LCLI-672's band work carried none either. The 0.13.0 section is LCLI-665's to write.

CONSISTENCY WITH QUEST-CLI, as measured rather than as relayed. The orchestrator's message said quest-cli's board band already renders the new line; quest-cli's `dev` does NOT carry it (its tip 0fc9eac2 has no `ctrl+x tab`, and `gh search code` over the repo returns nothing). The change is in flight in opum-ai/quest-cli#486's head, read by ref there: `<Text>Quest board ready · </Text>`, the `Open` Button on hotkey `o`, then `<Text> (ctrl+x tab, o)</Text>` with a test asserting `/\(ctrl\+x tab, o\)/`. This branch matches that shape. Their PR's own comment cites the ruling as seq 213 where ours is seq 212 -- their numbering, not a discrepancy in the change, and not worth a round trip.
finalSummary:
Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#482. The run that validated the deliverable is 37121080580, covering e2836c7f — cited rather than the merge SHA, which is post-merge by definition. All five criteria checked with evidence in hand; AC5 amended at closure to its own measurement rather than a weaker reading (the same change reddens no test that is not pre-existing, proven with a stashed control).

The band above the prompt now draws `Lore pane ready · [Open] (ctrl+x tab, o)`, so the affordance names the focus step its `o` hotkey needs, and a mod test pins the hint: removing it reddens exactly 1 of 57 tests, with the assertion naming the missing text. The skill text and docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md carry the same step.

Two things the next reader should have, both measured rather than assumed. `skills/lore/SKILL.md` is GENERATED — a hand-edit reddens test/plugin-skill.test.ts, and the change belongs in src/core/agent-bridge.ts followed by scripts/plugin-skill.ts --write. And the ubuntu CI leg is currently degrading: two of three attempts on this head were red with disjoint, all-timeout failure sets spanning suites the diff cannot reach, while the identical tree passed every one of those tests locally.
